name: Insecure Header Configuration - X-Frame-Options Missing/Permissive (ALLOW-FROM *)
description: ALLOW-FROM * permits framing from any origin, enabling clickjacking.
remediation: Use 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or a strict frame-ancestors CSP directive.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - Content-Security-Policy unsafe-inline + unsafe-eval
description: The CSP allows both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval, substantially weakening XSS mitigation.
remediation: Remove unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval; use nonces or hashes for required inline scripts.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - CSP Wildcard Source
description: A wildcard default-src in the CSP effectively disables the policy's origin restrictions.
remediation: Scope default-src to an explicit allow-list of trusted origins.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - Set-Cookie Missing Secure Flag over HTTPS
description: A cookie was set without the Secure flag, allowing it to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections if available.
remediation: Set the Secure attribute on all session/auth cookies.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - Set-Cookie Missing HttpOnly Flag
description: A session/auth cookie was set without HttpOnly, making it readable by client-side JavaScript and exploitable via XSS for session theft.
remediation: Set the HttpOnly attribute on all session/authentication cookies.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - Set-Cookie Missing SameSite Attribute
description: A session cookie lacks a SameSite attribute, increasing CSRF exposure in modern browsers' default-lax fallback scenarios.
remediation: Set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax explicitly on session cookies.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - Access-Control-Allow-Origin Wildcard with Credentials Risk
description: A wildcard CORS origin was returned; if combined with credentialed requests elsewhere this enables cross-origin data theft.
remediation: Replace wildcard CORS with an explicit allow-list of trusted origins.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - Strict-Transport-Security Short/Weak max-age
description: An HSTS max-age under 1000 seconds provides minimal protection against SSL-stripping downgrade attacks.
remediation: Set HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year) and include includeSubDomains/preload where appropriate.

name: Insecure Header Configuration - X-XSS-Protection Disabled
description: The legacy X-XSS-Protection header is explicitly disabled (though deprecated, its absence/disabling on legacy browsers removes a defense layer).
remediation: Rely on a strong CSP instead; if supporting legacy browsers, avoid explicitly disabling this header.

name: SSRF - AWS EC2 IMDS Metadata Credential Leak
description: A server-side request forgery payload caused the server to fetch the AWS EC2 IMDS instance metadata endpoint, leaking temporary cloud credentials directly into the response.
remediation: Block outbound requests to cloud metadata IP ranges (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal) at the application/network layer, enforce IMDSv2 (AWS), and validate/allow-list any user-supplied URLs used in server-side fetches.

name: Insecure Deserialization - Java (ysoserial-style)
description: A crafted Java (ysoserial-style) serialized-object payload triggered deserialization-related exceptions or class-loading errors in the response, indicating untrusted data reaches a native deserialization routine — a common RCE vector.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data with Java (ysoserial-style)'s native mechanism. Use safe, schema-validated formats (JSON/Protobuf) and allow-list permitted classes if native deserialization is unavoidable.

name: Open Redirect via Unvalidated next/return_url Parameter
description: A redirect parameter pointing to an external attacker-controlled domain caused the server to issue a 3xx redirect to that domain, which can be chained with phishing or OAuth token theft.
remediation: Validate redirect targets against an exact-match allow-list of internal paths/domains; never redirect to a raw user-supplied URL.

name: CRLF Injection / HTTP Response Splitting
description: A payload containing encoded CRLF sequences resulted in an injected header appearing in the raw response, confirming HTTP response splitting which can lead to cache poisoning, XSS, or session fixation.
remediation: Strictly validate and encode any user input placed into HTTP headers; use framework APIs that reject embedded CR/LF rather than building raw header strings.

name: Host Header Injection - Password Reset Poisoning
description: Submitting a forged Host header caused the server to reflect that attacker-controlled host back into the response body (e.g. in a generated link), indicating the application trusts the Host header for link generation — exploitable for password-reset poisoning and account takeover.
remediation: Never trust the Host header for generating absolute URLs/links. Use a fixed, server-side-configured canonical hostname instead.

name: HTTP Request Smuggling - Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding Discrepancy Indicator
description: A request containing both a Content-Length and a Transfer-Encoding: chunked header produced an unexpected response, which may indicate front-end/back-end parsing discrepancies exploitable for request smuggling. Manual confirmation with a differential timing test is required.
remediation: Ensure all components in the request chain (load balancer, CDN, app server) agree on a single, strict HTTP parsing standard; disable support for ambiguous Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length combinations.

name: Swagger/OpenAPI Specification Publicly Exposed
description: An OpenAPI/Swagger specification document is accessible, fully enumerating the API's endpoints, parameters, and (sometimes) internal-only routes.
remediation: Restrict access to API documentation endpoints in production to authenticated internal users, or remove them entirely from production builds.

name: GraphQL Batched Query Abuse Indicator
description: Submitting an array of repeated mutation/query objects in a single GraphQL request was accepted and processed without a batch-size limit, which can be abused to bypass rate limiting (e.g. for credential stuffing or coupon brute-forcing).
remediation: Enforce a strict maximum batch size per GraphQL request and apply rate limiting at the resolver level, not just per HTTP request.

name: GraphQL Field Suggestion Information Leak
description: Querying a deliberately misspelled field name caused the server to suggest the correct (real) field name in its error message, even with introspection disabled — leaking schema details.
remediation: Disable the 'did you mean' field-suggestion behavior in production GraphQL error formatting.

name: Actuator/Management Endpoint Exposure (Spring Boot)
description: A Spring Boot Actuator management endpoint (env, heapdump, beans, etc.) is publicly reachable, often exposing environment variables, credentials, or enabling remote code execution via the /jolokia or /env write endpoints.
remediation: Disable or restrict Actuator endpoints to an internal management port with authentication; never expose env/heapdump publicly.

name: JWT - Algorithm Confusion (RS256 to HS256)
description: A token re-signed as HS256 using the server's known RSA public key as the HMAC secret was accepted, confirming the verification logic does not enforce the expected signing algorithm — a critical authentication bypass (CVE-class jwt algorithm confusion).
remediation: Explicitly enforce and pin the expected JWT algorithm server-side; never derive the verification algorithm from the token's own header.

name: JWT - Kid Header SQL Injection / Path Traversal
description: A JWT with a manipulated 'kid' (key ID) header containing SQLi/path-traversal payloads caused a database error or file-read error, indicating the kid value is used unsafely to look up the verification key.
remediation: Validate the 'kid' header against a strict allow-list of known key identifiers before using it in any lookup; never use it directly in file paths or SQL queries.

name: JWT - Expired Token Still Accepted
description: A JWT with an 'exp' claim set far in the past was still accepted by the server (HTTP 200 authenticated response), confirming expiration is not enforced server-side.
remediation: Always validate the 'exp' (and 'nbf') claims server-side on every request, independent of client-side token handling.

name: Missing Rate Limit on OTP/2FA Verification Endpoint
description: Submitting 10 sequential incorrect OTP codes within the request window did not trigger a lockout, CAPTCHA, or 429 response, indicating the OTP endpoint can likely be brute-forced.
remediation: Implement strict, progressively-increasing rate limiting and account lockout/CAPTCHA on OTP and 2FA verification endpoints.

name: Price Manipulation via Client-Supplied Unit Price
description: An order/checkout request accepted a client-supplied 'price' field that overrode the server-computed catalog price, indicating price trust is misplaced on the client side.
remediation: Always recompute prices server-side from the authoritative product catalog at checkout time; never trust client-supplied price fields.

name: Workflow Step Skipping (Forced Browsing Past Payment)
description: Directly requesting a post-payment confirmation/fulfillment endpoint without a corresponding completed-payment state succeeded, indicating the application does not enforce workflow step ordering server-side.
remediation: Maintain server-side workflow/state machine validation for every multi-step process (e.g. checkout, onboarding) and reject requests that skip required prior steps.

name: Information Disclosure - Internal Hostname/FQDN Disclosure
description: The response body discloses internal hostname/fqdn disclosure, which can aid attacker reconnaissance or directly expose sensitive resources.
remediation: Strip internal identifiers, source paths, and infrastructure references from any response/error reachable by external clients.

name: Information Disclosure - Stack Trace Source Path Disclosure (Unix)
description: The response body discloses stack trace source path disclosure (unix), which can aid attacker reconnaissance or directly expose sensitive resources.
remediation: Strip internal identifiers, source paths, and infrastructure references from any response/error reachable by external clients.

name: Information Disclosure - Stack Trace Source Path Disclosure (Windows)
description: The response body discloses stack trace source path disclosure (windows), which can aid attacker reconnaissance or directly expose sensitive resources.
remediation: Strip internal identifiers, source paths, and infrastructure references from any response/error reachable by external clients.

name: Information Disclosure - Email Address Bulk Disclosure
description: The response body discloses email address bulk disclosure, which can aid attacker reconnaissance or directly expose sensitive resources.
remediation: Strip internal identifiers, source paths, and infrastructure references from any response/error reachable by external clients.

name: Information Disclosure - Internal API Endpoint Comment Disclosure
description: The response body discloses internal api endpoint comment disclosure, which can aid attacker reconnaissance or directly expose sensitive resources.
remediation: Strip internal identifiers, source paths, and infrastructure references from any response/error reachable by external clients.

name: Information Disclosure - Cloud Storage Bucket URL Disclosure (S3/GCS/Azure Blob)
description: The response body discloses cloud storage bucket url disclosure (s3/gcs/azure blob), which can aid attacker reconnaissance or directly expose sensitive resources.
remediation: Strip internal identifiers, source paths, and infrastructure references from any response/error reachable by external clients.

name: OAuth - PKCE Not Enforced on Authorization Code Flow
description: An authorization request using response_type=code did not include a code_challenge parameter, indicating PKCE is not enforced, leaving public clients (mobile/SPA) exposed to authorization code interception attacks.
remediation: Require code_challenge/code_challenge_method on every authorization request and reject code exchanges missing a matching code_verifier.

name: SAML - Signature Validation Bypass (XML Comment Injection)
description: Injecting an XML comment inside the NameID/Subject element of a SAML assertion was still accepted, suggesting the signature validation logic parses the element value with the comment stripped while the signature was computed on the original — a known SAML signature-wrapping bypass.
remediation: Use a SAML library that canonicalizes and validates the exact signed content, and reject assertions containing unexpected XML comments/extra elements inside signed nodes.

name: SSO - IDP-Initiated Login Without Audience Restriction Check
description: An assertion issued for a different intended audience (aud/Audience) was still accepted by this service provider, indicating cross-service assertion replay is possible.
remediation: Strictly validate the Audience/aud restriction in every SSO assertion against this exact service provider's entity ID.

name: Insecure File Upload - Double Extension Bypass (.php.jpg)
description: A file upload using the 'Double Extension Bypass (.php.jpg)' technique was accepted and the payload was later retrievable/executable, indicating insufficient server-side file-type and content validation.
remediation: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension/Content-Type) server-side, store uploads outside the web root with randomized names, and disable script execution in upload directories.

name: Insecure File Upload - Null Byte Extension Bypass
description: A file upload using the 'Null Byte Extension Bypass' technique was accepted and the payload was later retrievable/executable, indicating insufficient server-side file-type and content validation.
remediation: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension/Content-Type) server-side, store uploads outside the web root with randomized names, and disable script execution in upload directories.

name: Insecure File Upload - Content-Type Spoofing (image/jpeg with PHP payload)
description: A file upload using the 'Content-Type Spoofing (image/jpeg with PHP payload)' technique was accepted and the payload was later retrievable/executable, indicating insufficient server-side file-type and content validation.
remediation: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension/Content-Type) server-side, store uploads outside the web root with randomized names, and disable script execution in upload directories.

name: Insecure File Upload - SVG with Embedded Script (Stored XSS via Upload)
description: A file upload using the 'SVG with Embedded Script (Stored XSS via Upload)' technique was accepted and the payload was later retrievable/executable, indicating insufficient server-side file-type and content validation.
remediation: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension/Content-Type) server-side, store uploads outside the web root with randomized names, and disable script execution in upload directories.

name: Insecure File Upload - ZIP Path Traversal (Zip Slip)
description: A file upload using the 'ZIP Path Traversal (Zip Slip)' technique was accepted and the payload was later retrievable/executable, indicating insufficient server-side file-type and content validation.
remediation: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension/Content-Type) server-side, store uploads outside the web root with randomized names, and disable script execution in upload directories.

name: Prototype Pollution via __proto__ JSON Key
description: A JSON body containing a __proto__ key with a polluting value caused observable behavior change (e.g. reflected property on unrelated objects), indicating unsafe recursive merge/clone of user input pollutes Object.prototype — exploitable for DoS, auth bypass, or in some stacks RCE.
remediation: Use merge/clone libraries that explicitly block __proto__/constructor/prototype keys, or parse JSON with Object.create(null) prototypes; upgrade vulnerable lodash/jQuery/minimist versions.

name: Prototype Pollution via constructor.prototype JSON Key
description: A JSON body using the constructor.prototype path to pollute the base object prototype produced an observable side effect in the response, confirming an alternate prototype-pollution gadget chain beyond direct __proto__ filtering.
remediation: Block constructor/prototype/__proto__ keys at the deepest level of any recursive merge utility, not just the top level.

name: Web Cache Poisoning via X-Forwarded-Host
description: Injecting a forged X-Forwarded-Host header caused that value to be reflected into a cacheable response (e.g. a generated absolute link), which a CDN/cache could then serve to other users — enabling cache poisoning at scale.
remediation: Exclude unkeyed headers like X-Forwarded-Host from influencing cacheable response content, or include them in the cache key; validate the header against an allow-list.

name: Web Cache Deception - Sensitive Page Cached via Fake Static Extension
description: Appending a static-resource-like extension (e.g. /account/profile/nonexistent.css) to a sensitive authenticated page returned the sensitive content with cache-friendly headers, meaning a shared cache could store and later serve another user's private page.
remediation: Configure the cache layer to key on the full path/extension correctly and never cache responses containing Set-Cookie or Vary: Cookie content based on path-extension heuristics alone.

name: Deprecated/Unversioned API Path Still Reachable
description: A response was served from a legacy/unversioned API path (e.g. /api/v1/ alongside a current /api/v3/), which often receives less security review and weaker authorization enforcement than the current version.
remediation: Retire deprecated API versions entirely rather than leaving them reachable, or apply identical authorization middleware to all active versions.

name: Object-Level Authorization Hint - Resource Owner ID Mismatch in Response
description: The response includes both a resource's owner_id/user_id field and what appears to be the requesting session's own identifier in proximity, with mismatched values — a strong indicator that object-level authorization (BOLA) was not enforced for this resource. Confirm by replaying as the owning user.
remediation: Enforce object-level authorization on every resource-returning endpoint: verify the authenticated principal owns or is permitted to access the specific object ID requested, not just that they are authenticated.

name: Sensitive Action Page Frameable (Clickjacking)
description: A page that appears to perform a sensitive state-changing action (form with submit-type inputs) was served without X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors CSP directive, leaving it embeddable in an attacker's iframe for clickjacking.
remediation: Send X-Frame-Options: DENY or a frame-ancestors 'none'/'self' CSP directive on all pages that trigger state-changing actions.

name: Subdomain Takeover Indicator - GitHub Pages
description: A response consistent with an unclaimed GitHub Pages resource was returned for this hostname, indicating a dangling DNS record (CNAME) pointing to a deprovisioned GitHub Pages resource that an attacker could claim and use for phishing/session theft under your domain.
remediation: Remove the dangling DNS record pointing to the deprovisioned GitHub Pages resource, or reclaim/reconfigure the resource immediately.
